labDirector.title: Principal Investigator
labDirector.name: Jennifer Hong, MD
labDirector.description: I am a neurosurgeon-scientist who works at the intersection of patient care, regenerative medicine, transcriptomics and advanced bioimaging. The goal of my lab is to use cutting-edge scientific tools to solve clinically-relevant problems and better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal disfunction, degeneration and repair in patients. Ultimately, I hope to improve patient outcomes for neurosurgical interventions in the areas of epilepsy and peripheral nerve injury. I believe that research makes a difference, and a central focus of my lab is scientific mentorship and training of the next generation of biomedical researchers.

people.name: Vishva Natarajan
people.description: I’m a bioinformatician and medical student developing computational platforms that bring data-driven precision to patient care. My work integrates deep learning and computational pathology, including VirtualPNN, a generative AI framework for label-free visualization of perineuronal nets in the brain tumor microenvironment. When I'm not writing loss functions or studying for boards, I enjoy practicing my latte art, designing menus for dinner parties, and rocking my electric guitar.

people.name: Charles Mazof
people.description: I am a medical student in the Class of 2028 with interests in neuroimmunology, cell genetics, and disease mechanisms. I have a background in molecular biology and machine learning, particularly applied to single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin epigenetics. Currently, I am using these techniques to investigate diseased cell states in focal cortical dysplasias.

people.name: Jacob Fredman
people.description: I am a medical student at the Geisel School of Medicine. Originally from Tucson, Arizona, I enjoy spending my free time outdoors, especially hiking, swimming, and skiing. I also enjoy cooking and baking.

people.name: Theodore Kapogiannis
people.description: After earning a degree in Biometry and Statistics, I joined a management consulting firm, where I gained exposure to global healthcare systems and the pharmaceutical industry. I then spent two years conducting research in Parkinson’s disease, neurosurgery, and artificial intelligence. Through these experiences, I developed an interest in functional neurosurgery and how healthcare system–level factors influence care delivery. At the Hong Lab, I study predictors of patient outcomes following epilepsy surgery.

people.name: Xavier Takam
people.description: I am a current medical student at the Geisel School of Medicine and interested in becoming a neurosurgeon. More specifically, I am interested in optimizing care for patients suffering from strokes and other vascular pathologies of the brain. I feel fortunate to be part of the Hong Lab and have already learned a lot since starting. In the lab, I focus on understanding how recent advances have impacted stroke care. Outside of medicine, I have multiple interests including business and sports although most of my time is spent enjoying the company of my family and loved ones.

people.name: Dara Cuffe
people.description: I have been interested in bettering therapeutics for brain pathologies for several years. Previously, I researched microglia and CNS drug delivery at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard and more broadly at Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, where I worked in extrahepatic delivery and emerging medicines. I ran the Boston Marathon for the Alzheimer’s Association and ran Division 1 cross-country, indoor, & outdoor track. I have tested more than a hundred New York Times Cooking recipes and countless local and regional coffee rosters. I create jewelry, do woodworking, and paddle board through Dartmouth as well. In the lab, I work with the NIS database. I helped start up human organotypic slices using tissue resected during underutilized procedures that can cure epilepsy called lobectomies. I hope to improve patient care and therapeutics through these two avenues for the rest of my time here!

people.name: Brizha Knowles
people.description: I am a fourth-year medical student at the Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth with research interests in clinical neurosurgery, translational neuroscience, neuro-oncology, neurotrauma, and peripheral nerve injury. My current research focuses on whole-body fluorescence cryotomography to map AAV tropism and delivery, as well as preclinical studies of diabetic peripheral neuropathy and nerve regeneration.

people.name: Dhanya Mahesh
people.description: I am a fourth-year medical student at Dartmouth. My research investigates neuronal signaling and perineuronal net morphology in human brain organotypic slice cultures as a model system for studying epilepsy.

people.name: Petra Bachanova
people.description: I'm a third-year PhD student in the Integrative Neuroscience department, co-advised by Dr Hong and Dr Jobst. My research focuses on patients with medication-resistant epilepsy who are candidates for surgical brain resection. I use genomic and electrophysiological approaches to better understand seizure generation and predict outcomes after surgery. Outside the lab, you'll find me in the mountains, be it skiing, trail running, cycling, or climbing!

people.name: Kylie Nelson-Marois
people.description: I am a PhD student in the IND program. Prior to Dartmouth, I earned my BA and MA at Wesleyan University, studying the effects of SSRIs on zebra finch neurogenesis. In the Hong lab, my research interests include studying the pathogenesis of drug-resistant epilepsy and applying this knowledge to engineer new medical technologies. Outside of the lab, I enjoy hiking, lifting, indie video games, and collecting knickknacks like art, trinkets & vinyl.

people.name: Ahmad Wahab
people.description: Hi, I am Ahmad Wahab, a computational tech assistant in Hong Lab. I am passionate about leveraging technology to advance neuroscience research and improve patient outcomes.

people.name: Sydney Park
people.description: I am an undergraduate student in the Class of 2029 at Dartmouth College studying cognitive science, medicine, and Spanish, and I figure skate for DFSC. I have previously researched neurodegenerative diseases and read-through compounds, and I am currently assisting with an EpoB project, specifically working on mice behavior and health.
